rv.q: Honestly, I'm not mad about it.
The show ticks all the boxes that devotees of the movie will want and expect, while never really establishing a reason for being of its own.
Generic songs, a derivative script and a daunting act to follow add up to a film-to-stage adaptation that’s shiny but skimpy
But none of the characters on stage feel real or alive.
this show doesn’t really have a soul of its own
When the musical embraces camp, it does it well.
Despite songs from Elton John, this stage adaptation of the classic millennial film is a decent comedy but a lousy musical
If only this fabulousness could extend to director Jerry Mitchell’s choreography, which is bewilderingly and irredeemably naff, like a local Zumba class attempting a line dance.
Sparkly as it is, I fear Miranda would hang it back on the rail.
As a musical it’s pretty and uninteresting, shot through with the kind of obviousness and mediocrity that Miranda Priestly would abhor.
This musical feels...neither aspirational nor memorable enough to escape the sale rack.
The Devil Wears Prada is a visually striking and musically catchy show that will appeal to fans of the original material and anyone in search of a glamorous, escapist night at the theatre.

There is more than enough on offer here to provide a perfectly fun Saturday night out, but despite its repeated championing of fashion as an art rather than just a cynical business, this musical's lack of distinct innovation might lead some to construe its production as somewhat cynical itself.
Here, as elsewhere, you get the feeling of a production too often settling for the generic when only true gorgeousness will do.
